summary: A well-architected Phase 2 with two defects that go to the heart of the phase. The graph is right: one AudioContext (instrumented constructor, count=1), per-layer buses in the documented order, reverb before a shared rotary, one destination; Master Level (1.0->0.2 = -13.98 dB vs ideal -13.98) and the layer faders are exact. All six piano types are measurably distinct, three of them genuine bundled CC-BY sample sets that load offline, with a real labeled fallback when the assets are blocked. Focus/group/global targeting is correct to the sample. But Mod 2's LFO is never connected to its modulation gain (effects.ts has no lfo.connect(lfoGain), unlike Mod 1), so nothing in Mod 2 modulates: Chorus and Ensemble render bit-identical to bypass (residual 0.0000, xcorr 1.0000) and Spin sits at the take-to-take floor. The Amp Sim voicing gains are overwritten by the EQ knobs at centre, so Twin/JC/Small are one sound (Small vs JC residual 0.0000). String Res changes nothing at all, sustain exists only over MIDI CC64, and a 20-note synth chord peaks at 3.291 with 19,238 clipped samples past the limiter. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares several of these as working.

criteria.label: Instrument breadth & character
evidence: All six types are measurably distinct in the running build. Pairwise normalised spectral L1 on a C4 take (0 = identical): Grand/Upright 0.643, Grand/Electric 0.941, Grand/Clav 1.370, Electric/Digital 0.249 (closest pair), Grand/Misc 1.282. Nothing is one voice relabelled.

Grand, Upright and Electric really are recorded: build/samples/{grand,upright,electric} each hold 30 mp3 root notes A0..C8 a minor third apart with a manifest.json, and the page loads them from the local build with no network (status chip reads 'Piano ready (recorded + synth voices)'). Their spectra track the declared FluidR3_GM programs (grand / honkytonk / electric_piano_1).

Character is simplified in ways a player notices. The Digital voice is a 3-partial triangle+sine stack with no decay stage (src/audio/sampler.ts SynthVoice applies a percussive ramp only for 'mallet' and 'clav'): measured RMS was 0.14716 / 0.14726 / 0.14725 at C3/C4/C5 and the envelope stays flat until release, so a 'Digital Grand' sustains like an organ. Clav is saw+square, Misc is three sines.
Only one recorded velocity layer per root note (declared honestly), so loudness scaling is the whole dynamic story for the sampled sets.

Level between families is badly mismatched at identical settings: single C4 peak was Grand 0.024828, Upright 0.026299, Electric 0.028996 versus Clav 0.279951, Digital 0.405103, Misc 0.620304 - a ~28 dB jump on a type change (charged mainly under signalGraph).

criteria.label: Effect audibility & correctness
evidence: Mod 2 does not modulate at all. src/audio/effects.ts builds Mod2Unit's oscillator and its lfoGain but never writes `this.lfo.connect(this.lfoGain)` (Mod1Unit does, at line 110), so lfoGain is a gain node with no input and delayTime/allpass frequency receive zero modulation. Measured against a warmed-up baseline with the unit engaged: Chorus residual 0.0000 / xcorr 1.0000 / dRMS 0.00 dB, Ensemble residual 0.0000 / xcorr 1.0000, Spin residual 0.0085 - the take-to-take determinism floor was 0.0000. Three of six required Mod 2 types are inaudible; Flanger (residual 0.2765), Phaser (0.4328) and Vibe (0.5515) survive only as static comb/all-pass colour with no sweep.

Amp Sim's three amp models are one sound. controlBindings.ts calls engine.setAmpModel(...) and then setBass/setMid/setTreble from the panel knobs, whose centre positions ramp the voicing gains applyRouting just set back to 0 dB. Measured: Small vs JC residual 0.0000 / xcorr 1.0000 / dRMS 0.00 dB; Small vs Twin residual 0.0113 (-39 dB). The effects spec states the three 'must not sound identical'. LP24 vs HP24 do differ strongly (residual 0.9596, dRMS -14.99 dB).

Mod 1 is the healthy unit: Ring Mod residual 1.2221 / xcorr 0.0061, Tremolo 0.3237, A-Pan 0.2453 (channel correlation 0.355 vs -0.032 bypassed), Wah 0.4269 / specL1 0.7289, Pump 0.4520, and Trem vs Pump residual 0.2204 - all six audible and distinct. A-Wah is not an envelope follower though: effects.ts handles 'A-Wah' in the same case as 'Wah' with a smaller LFO depth.

Delay, Compressor, Reverb and Rotary all process real audio. Delay with feedback 0.8 stretched the 10%-decay point from 34 to 62-69 envelope frames and the three feedback filters differ (LP/HP/BP residuals 0.524/0.312/0.378 with distinct envelope shapes), confirming the filter sits inside the loop. Reverb decay ordering is right (Booth 29 frames < Room 31 < Stage 40 < Spring 43 < Cathedral 58 < Hall 71) and Bright vs Dark moves the 6.5 kHz band from 1.03e-6 to 1.80e-7 (~15 dB). Reverb dry/wet at 0 returns the dry signal (residual 0.0085). Rotary reached from To Rotary gives slow vs fast residual 0.3442 with side energy 0.18 vs a 0.007 baseline.
The Compressor is mostly a level control: amount 0 -> 1 added +21.5 dB RMS while the envelope ripple only fell from 1.387 to 1.314. Fast mode does change the result (residual vs slow 0.4226).
All-effects bypass works: with Mod 1 + Reverb engaged, turning the Layer Effects ON pill off returned the signal to within 0.02 dB of the un-effected baseline.

criteria.label: Signal graph & gain staging
evidence: Exactly one AudioContext and one destination path. Instrumenting window.AudioContext and AudioNode.prototype.connect in the served build gave audioContexts=1, sampleRate 48000, and the only app node reaching ctx.destination was a DynamicsCompressorNode (the master limiter); the second destination connection was my own recording tap.

Chain order matches the contract - input -> Mod1 -> Mod2 -> Delay -> Amp/EQ -> Comp -> Reverb -> level -> master -> limiter -> destination (audioEngine.ts LayerChain), with the shared Rotary fed post-reverb so reverb always precedes rotary, verified behaviourally by selecting To Rotary and hearing the rotor (side energy 0.18 vs 0.007).

Gain law is exact where it is implemented: Master Level 1.0 -> 0.2 measured -13.98 dB (ideal -13.98); layer A fader 0.85 -> 0.30 measured -9.06 dB (ideal -9.04); enabling layer B at 0.4 then raising it to 1.0 gave +3.33 dB then +3.41 dB, total +6.74 dB against the +6.76 dB a coherent sum predicts.

It clips hard under load. Recording at the destination (post-limiter), a 20-key chord on Misc peaked at 3.291 with 19,238 samples at or beyond full scale; the worst case I could build from the panel (Digital, both layers, all six units engaged, master 1.0) peaked at 2.702 with 27,045 clipped samples. The limiter is a DynamicsCompressor at threshold -3 dB / ratio 12 / 3 ms attack, which does not stop +10 dBFS overs.

Staging inside the chain is equally uncalibrated: engaging Amp Sim/EQ at its default drive of 0.3 adds +28.2 dB (peak 0.0248 -> 0.3232) because a fixed k=50 soft-clip curve is driven by pre-gain, and Compressor amount adds +21.5 dB. Meanwhile the sampled instruments idle at -32 dBFS peak for a single note, so the headroom is spent in the wrong places.

Voices and nodes are cleaned up: 100 down/up pairs in 128 ms left 0 stuck voices, the blur handler took the voice count 1 -> 0, and the section ON button produced exact digital silence (peak 0.000000).

criteria.label: Two-layer piano behaviour
evidence: Enable, level, octave and focus all reach the audio graph. Layer B ON added +3.33 dB, B's fader 0.4 -> 1.0 added a further +3.41 dB (coherent-sum prediction +6.76 dB), turning layer A off left B alone (residual 0.9901 vs the two-layer take), and Piano section OFF gave exact silence.

Octave shift is per focused layer: after pressing FOCUS B (which also moved the FX FOCUS selector to 'Piano B'), two OCTAVE-up presses changed only B (residual 0.5639, specL1 0.3556 toward the upper bands) while A kept playing at pitch.

FX focus targeting is exact. With focus on A I engaged an HP24 amp (layer A residual 0.9954, -14.27 dB); layer B alone then rendered bit-identical to the pre-edit baseline (residual 0.0000, xcorr 1.0000). Turning GROUP on propagated the same edit to B, and a GLOBAL reverb reached B while the same reverb without GLOBAL did not.

The panel tracks state: faders and knobs expose aria-valuenow/aria-valuetext that follow the value ('Piano layer A level' 85%, 'Master Level' 70%), selectors relabel themselves ('Reverb type: Cath', 'FX focus: Piano B'), buttons carry aria-pressed and lit LEDs.

The significant simplification: both layers share one piano type and one set of performance controls (controlBindings.ts applies setPerformance globally, not per layer), so A and B can only ever be the same sound at different levels and octaves - the two-layer feature a Stage 4 player would use to stack a Grand under an EP is not available.

criteria.label: Detailed piano controls
evidence: Measured against a determinism floor of residual 0.0084 established by two identical takes: KB Touch Heavy -1.46 dB / Light +1.10 dB; Dyn Comp 1 +0.50 dB and 3 +1.45 dB; Timbre Soft/Mid/Bright specL1 0.1921 / 0.1098 / 0.2125; Unison 1 xcorr 0.1514 and Unison 3 xcorr 0.0550; Soft Release residual 0.1168 with a visibly longer release tail. Five of the six required detail controls do change rendered signal.

String Res is dead. Engaging it produced residual 0.0084, xcorr 1.0000, dRMS -0.02 dB - exactly the determinism floor. The source agrees: `stringRes` appears only in the control definition, controlBindings.ts and the PerformanceParams field; it is never read by voiceParams or any audio node (SampledVoice/SynthVoice never see it). The piano spec lists String Res as required and its acceptance criteria say it must measurably change rendered audio.

Sustain is reachable only over MIDI CC64. There is no UI pedal control on the panel (the only sustain-named controls are the per-section SUSTPED routing toggles) and useKeyboardInput/keyboardMap.ts contain no sustain key at all. Holding Space over a note with focus cleared left the signal at residual 0.0138 / xcorr 0.9999 versus the same note with no key held, and the envelope tail was zero in both. The piano spec requires UI control, keyboard mapping and CC64.

Unison costs level rather than adding it: Unison 1 measured -2.92 dB and Unison 3 -7.12 dB, because each voice is divided by voiceCount with no correlation compensation, so the widest setting is also the quietest.
Pedal Noise is inert too (residual 0.0084, identical to the floor). The piano spec does exclude pedal noise, so a decorative control is legitimate - but it is not listed anywhere as unsupported.

criteria.label: Input reliability & failure behaviour
evidence: Pointer, multi-touch and computer keyboard all reach one shared lifecycle (NoteRouter with per-owner tags), and the 20-key chord test showed deterministic oldest-first stealing: 20 held keys reported 17 live voices against a 16-per-layer cap, with no runaway.

Cleanup is solid: the blur handler took the voice count from 1 to 0, and 100 keydown/keyup pairs fired in 128 ms left 0 voices and a post-stress take bit-identical to the pre-stress baseline (peak 0.024828 both).

Failures degrade visibly. Blocking /samples/** at the network layer put the app into status 'fallback' with the strip reading 'Playable fallback (synthesized; samples unavailable)' and it stayed playable (peak 0.405). Web MIDI in this browser reported denied and the strip honestly read 'MIDI denied' rather than claiming a connection; the CC64 path exists in src/input/midi.ts and is unit-tested but I could not exercise a live device.

It does fail silently once: 60 back-to-back keydown/keyup pairs with no gap threw two uncaught 'Minified React error #185' (maximum update depth) page errors with no visible indication. At a musical rate (40 notes at ~8/s) the console stayed clean, and audio recovered fully afterwards.
Note repeat is suppressed via a held-code set and typing targets are excluded, so autorepeat does not double-trigger.

criteria.label: Required piano instruments
evidence: All six required types are on the PIANO SELECT selector and every one selects a playable model in the served build - I cycled Grand/Upright/Electric/Clav/Digital/Misc and recorded a sounding note for each at C3, C4 and C5 (RMS 0.0019 to 0.148).

The three recorded sets exist in the published build and load offline: build/samples/{grand,upright,electric} with 30 mp3 root notes each plus manifest.json, index.json and LICENSE.txt, and full provenance (FluidR3_GM, CC-BY-3.0, gleitz/midi-js-soundfonts) in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json.
The labeled fallback required by the spec works: with the sample directory blocked the status attribute became 'fallback' and the strip said so, and notes still sounded from the synthesized recipe.

The MODEL dial does nothing. It renders as role=spinbutton 'Piano model dial', but ControlView wires the encoder to onStep={() => {}}; six ArrowUp steps changed the rendered audio by residual 0.0000 / xcorr 1.0000. One model per type is allowed by the spec as an optional extra, but the dial itself is inert and undeclared.

The Program OLED never reports the loaded model. It is static markup reading 'A:11 / Nord Stage 4 / B3 Soulful / White Grand / Vista Pad Whl' regardless of the selected type, so the spec's modelNameShownInProgramDisplay and the missing-model reporting behaviour are not met; the six-LED type list is the only feedback.

criteria.label: Required effect units and types
evidence: All six units plus the shared Rotary are on the panel and reachable, with per-unit ON, ALL FX OFF, the section ON pill, FX FOCUS (7 entries), manual FOCUS A/B, GROUP, and GLOBAL on Delay/Compressor/Reverb - and I confirmed focus, group and global all change which chain an edit lands on.
Type coverage is complete for Mod 1 (RM/Trem/A-Pan/A-Wah/Wah/Pump), Mod 2 (Chor/Flang/Phas/Vibe/Ens/Spin) and Reverb (Room/Stage/Booth/Hall/Spring/Cath).

Amp Sim/EQ ships 6 of the spec's 7 types: the panel list is ['Small','JC','Twin','To Rotary','LP Filter','HP Filter'] (src/model/controls.ts), so 'EQ only' has no panel position and is unreachable even though effects.ts defines it.

The Delay feedback filter selector offers only LP/HP/BP; the spec's 'Off' position is missing, so the repeats can never be left unfiltered. Delay TAP/SET is inert - controlBindings.ts never reads 'effects-delay-tap', and neither Mod 1 nor Delay exposes the spec-listed Master Clock sync.

Rotary is only half-bound: applyEffectParams reads drive and speed, so the Rotary ON button, stop mode, source and morph buttons on the Performance section change nothing. The Delay 'EFFECTS' selector exposes the spec-excluded Chor/Vibe/Ens/Flam/Space list and is unbound.

criteria.label: Declared gaps are accurate
evidence: The parts of the declaration I could check about sources are true. Grand/Upright/Electric really are bundled recordings with the stated 30 root notes and licence, Clav/Digital/Misc really are runtime synthesis, and the reverb impulses really are generated. The decorative claim also holds: moving organ drawbars, ORGAN ON, the synth filter knob and SYNTH ON changed the rendered audio by residual 0.0000 / xcorr 1.0000.
But functional.piano lists 'String Res' among the working controls, and it measurably does nothing (residual 0.0084 = the determinism floor; no audio node ever reads the flag).
audio.strategy and functional.keybed both claim 'sustain (UI/keyboard/MIDI CC64)'. There is no UI sustain control and no keyboard sustain mapping; only CC64 exists.

The notes claim 'all units process real audio with working bypass and dry/wet' and that every Layer-Effects control measurably changes rendered audio. Mod 2 Chorus and Ensemble are bit-identical to bypass and the three amp models are one sound, so that claim is false as written. The candidate's own tests/effects.test.ts only asserts `unique.size >= 3` across six Mod 2 types, which is why this passed the gate.

decorativeControls names only Organ, Synth and Program, yet these Piano/Effects/Performance controls are also inert and undeclared: piano-ped-noise, piano-info, piano-model, effects-delay-type, effects-delay-tap, performance-rotary-on/stopmode/source/morph.

The Phase 2 outcome makes Panic-equivalent cleanup real, but the PANIC button is unbound: with a note held the voice count stayed at 1 after pressing it. Blur/unmount cleanup does work, so the behaviour exists - just not on the button, and the gap is not declared.

issues.title: Mod 2's LFO is never connected, so half its types are inaudible
issues.detail: src/audio/effects.ts constructs Mod2Unit's OscillatorNode and its lfoGain but never calls this.lfo.connect(this.lfoGain) - Mod1Unit does exactly that at line 110. lfoGain therefore has no input and contributes silence to delay.delayTime and allpass.frequency, so no Mod 2 type modulates. Measured in the published build against a warmed-up baseline with the unit engaged and default rate/amount: Chorus residual 0.0000 / xcorr 1.0000 / dRMS 0.00 dB, Ensemble residual 0.0000 / xcorr 1.0000, Spin residual 0.0085 (the take-to-take floor was 0.0000). Because the wet/dry mixer goes fully wet when a unit is engaged, a static delay line is exactly the dry signal, so Chorus and Ensemble are literally no-ops. Flanger, Phaser and Vibe still colour the signal (residual 0.2765 / 0.4328 / 0.5515) but as fixed comb and all-pass filters with no sweep. This fails the phase hard gate that each effect unit and type must process real audio, and it is contradicted by IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json's claim that all units process real audio.

issues.title: Twin, JC and Small render identically
issues.detail: AmpEqUnit.applyRouting sets the per-model voicing (Twin treble +4/mid -2, JC treble +6/bass +2, Small mid +4/treble -3), but controlBindings.applyEffectParams calls setAmpModel and then immediately setBass/setMid/setTreble from the panel knobs, whose default centre position ramps every one of those gains to 0 dB within 20 ms. Measured: Small vs JC residual 0.0000 / xcorr 1.0000 / dRMS 0.00 dB; Small vs Twin residual 0.0113 (-39 dB, below audibility). The effects spec states explicitly that the three amps 'must not sound identical'. Additionally the spec's seventh type, 'EQ only', has no panel position at all (src/model/controls.ts lists six) so it is unreachable.

issues.title: Hard clipping at the destination under polyphonic load
issues.detail: Recording at ctx.destination (post-limiter), a 20-key chord on the Misc voice peaked at 3.291 with 19,238 samples at or beyond full scale, and the worst case reachable from the panel (Digital, both layers enabled, all six units engaged, master 1.0) peaked at 2.702 with 27,045 clipped samples. The master limiter is a DynamicsCompressorNode at threshold -3 dB, ratio 12, 3 ms attack with the default soft knee, which cannot hold +10 dBFS transients. The root cause is uncalibrated staging: a single Grand note peaks at 0.0248 (-32 dBFS) while a single Misc note peaks at 0.6203, a ~28 dB spread on a type change, and engaging Amp Sim/EQ at its default drive adds another +28.2 dB while Compressor amount adds +21.5 dB.

issues.title: String Res is wired to nothing but declared functional
issues.detail: The STRING RES button toggles, lights its LED and reaches PerformanceParams.stringRes, but no audio node ever reads it: the flag appears only in src/model/controls.ts, src/audio/controlBindings.ts (lines 68 and 208) and src/audio/audioEngine.ts (the field declaration and its default) - voiceParams() does not pass it and neither SampledVoice nor SynthVoice references it. Engaging it in the published build gave residual 0.0084, xcorr 1.0000, dRMS -0.02 dB, identical to my two-identical-takes determinism floor. The piano spec lists String Res as required and its acceptance criteria demand it measurably change rendered audio, and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json's functional.piano lists it among the working controls.

issues.title: Sustain has no UI control and no keyboard mapping, but is declared as having both
issues.detail: The piano spec requires sustain from a UI control, a keyboard mapping and MIDI CC64; IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json claims 'sustain (UI/keyboard/MIDI CC64)' in audio.strategy and 'CC64 sustain' in functional.keybed. In the build only CC64 exists. src/input/keyboardMap.ts maps notes only, useKeyboardInput.ts installs no sustain handler, and the only sustain-named panel controls are the per-section SUSTPED routing toggles. Holding Space over a note with focus cleared left the rendered signal at residual 0.0138 / xcorr 0.9999 against the same note played with nothing held, and both envelope tails decayed to zero at the same time.

issues.title: Both piano layers share one type and one set of performance controls
issues.detail: controlBindings.applyAll calls engine.setPerformance once with the single panel state, so piano type, KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre, Unison and Soft Release are global rather than per layer. Layer A and B can differ only in enable, level and octave - measured as a pure coherent sum (+6.74 dB with B at full against a predicted +6.76 dB, xcorr 1.0000 with layer A alone). Stacking two different piano sounds, the main musical use of the two layers, is not possible.

issues.title: Several listed effect parameters are inert or absent
issues.detail: Delay TAP/SET is never read by controlBindings.applyEffectParams; the Delay feedback-filter selector omits the spec's 'Off' position (only LP/HP/BP); Master Clock sync is absent from both Mod 1 and Delay; and of the Rotary's listed parameters only drive and speed are bound, so the Rotary ON button, stop mode, source and morph buttons on the Performance section change nothing. The Delay 'EFFECTS' selector exposes the spec-excluded Chor/Vibe/Ens/Flam/Space list and is likewise unbound.

issues.title: Inert Piano, Effects and Performance controls are not listed as unsupported
issues.detail: decorativeControls in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json names only Organ, Synth and Program, but these are inert too and undeclared: piano-ped-noise (measured residual 0.0084, the determinism floor), piano-info, piano-model (six ArrowUp steps gave residual 0.0000), effects-delay-type, effects-delay-tap, and performance-rotary-on/stopmode/source/morph. PANIC is also unbound - with a note held, pressing it left the voice count at 1 - although the Phase 2 outcome asks for Panic-equivalent cleanup to become real (blur and unmount cleanup do work).

issues.title: Uncaught React 'maximum update depth' error under burst input
issues.detail: 60 back-to-back keydown/keyup pairs dispatched with no gap produced two uncaught page errors, 'Minified React error #185' (maximum update depth exceeded), with no visible indication in the UI. At a musical rate (40 notes at roughly 8 per second) the console stayed clean, and the app recovered completely - a post-stress take was bit-identical to the pre-stress baseline and no voices were stuck. Likely the per-note setActiveNotes update from NoteRouter.subscribe.

issues.title: Program OLED never reports the loaded piano model
issues.detail: src/components/Oled.tsx renders fixed markup ('A:11 / Nord Stage 4 / B3 Soulful / White Grand / Vista Pad Whl') for the Program display, so the model name does not follow the PIANO SELECT type and the spec's missing-model reporting behaviour has nowhere to appear. Verified by reading the OLED text with Grand selected and again after cycling the type. The six-LED type list beside the selector is the only model feedback the panel gives.

issues.title: pnpm run lint does not reproduce on a clean install
issues.detail: Portability note, not a gate failure. On a fresh `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` of the sealed artifact, `pnpm run test` (126 tests, 15 files), `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run build` all pass, but `pnpm run lint` exits 1: the artifact ships no oxlint ignore configuration, so oxlint walks node_modules and emits ~45,000 warnings from the bundled typescript.js. Linting the candidate's own code (`oxlint src tests`) exits 0 with three unicorn/no-useless-spread warnings, so the source itself is clean.
